Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate you sharing the high-level goals for FinWave's customer-support summarization and extraction pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get an apples-to-apples eval running:

Summary from discovery:
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support transcripts (avg 1.2k tokens, 95th 3.5k).
- Success metrics: accuracy on entity extraction (precision/recall), instruction-following quality (human eval pass rate), and latency under 500ms p50 for short responses.
- Constraint: target infra = a dedicated GPU pool with cost sensitive throughput (target < $0.0009/token).

Initial model recommendations (for eval):
1) Llama-2-Chat-70B (fp16) — baseline for quality.
2) LLaMA-2-13B-AWQ — strong quality/throughput tradeoff; AWQ often gives 2–2.5x throughput vs GPTQ with near-baseline quality in instruction tasks.
3) Mistral-7B-GPTQ — lower-cost option for high-throughput batch scoring.

Quantization trade study we discussed: AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8. Attached a short trade study (awq_vs_gptq_tradeoffs.pdf) and the prompt/test set we captured during the call (finwave_prompt_set_v2.json). Key notes from our internal experiments:
- AWQ: +2–2.5x throughput, ~1–2% drop on automated instruction metrics for some instruction-heavy prompts; often indistinguishable in human eval for domain prompts after light prompt-engineering.
- GPTQ: solid middle ground; slightly lower throughput than AWQ but more stable across edge-case prompts.
- FP8: can reduce memory footprint significantly (enables larger batch sizes) but we've seen occasional quality regressions on very long-context, numeracy-sensitive tasks.

Proposed eval plan (2 weeks minimum, ideally 7–14 days):
- Run the three model configs above on FinWave prompt set (attached).
- Metrics: per-prompt correctness (custom rubric), human-rated instruction pass rate, latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens.
- Acceptance criteria: human pass rate within 3% of fp16 baseline + latency/cost targets.

Next steps / ask from you:
1) Confirm the prompt/test set in the attachment is representative or share a sanitized sample to run at-scale.
2) Provide an S3 link or share via Drive for a ~1k-record test set (can be pseudonymized).
3) Approve the 2-week eval window and a short kick-off call with Rishi (SE) to validate configs.

Happy to set this up — suggested 30-min slot Wed/Thu this week.

Thanks,

Samir — quick technical notes below to address your questions. I'm happy to run numbers during the eval.

Throughput (approx, single A100 40GB, inference runtime tuned):
- Llama-2-Chat-70B fp16: ~850–1,100 tokens/sec for short seqs ( batching enabled, KV cache hot )
- LLaMA-2-13B-AWQ: ~1,800–2,200 tokens/sec (AWQ memory layout + int8 compute paths)
- LLaMA-2-13B-GPTQ: ~1,300–1,600 tokens/sec

Notes on quality regressions and where they show up:
- AWQ: most regressions are on long-context numerical precision and some deterministic extraction tasks (dates, amounts). Observed automated metric drops ~1–3% on a handful of templates; human eval difference often <1% after prompt adjustments.
- GPTQ: fewer regressions vs AWQ on extraction tasks but slightly lower best-case throughput.
- FP8: avoids some AWQ/GPTQ failure modes but can induce instability on very deep attention patterns (rare).

Mitigation strategies we recommend:
- Start with AWQ for the non-critical inference path to get throughput/cost wins.
- For safety-sensitive extraction (dates/amounts), run a small fp16 fallback path (costly but only executed on small subset flagged by heuristics). We can wire this in as a two-tier inference policy in Redwood (fast quant model -> fallback to fp16 for low-confidence outputs).
- Per-prompt evaluation: we recommend a checklist-driven eval that includes automated extraction accuracy, instruction-pass rate, and a 50-sample human spot-check focused on numeracy and hallucination.

I'll prepare a short notebook we can run that outputs per-prompt delta vs fp16 and a suggested confidence threshold for fallback. Link to a draft benchmark: https://redwood.internal/evals/benchmarks/finwave-quantization (will push after kick-off).

—Rishi
